title: Automate security-questionnaire responses + pricing addendum templates to speed enterprise procurement
creator: Priya Menon
description: Problem: Enterprise deals frequently stall during procurement due to repetitive security questionnaires and bespoke pricing addenda. Current process: sales collects SSO/SOC2 artifacts manually, legal drafts addenda per deal, and security fields repeated across questionnaires. This adds ~2-6 weeks to close and increases legal effort. Goal: build a combined approach that (1) standardizes a set of approved pricing addendum templates tied to commitment tiers, (2) automates answers to the top 40 security questionnaire questions with links to living SOC2 evidence, and (3) surfaces a self-serve vendor evidence portal for Sales/Procurement/Customer to reference during negotiation. Success metrics: reduce procurement time for enterprise P0 deals by 30% and decrease legal addendum drafts by 50% in first quarter after launch.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A set of 3 pricing addendum templates (monthly, annual, reserved capacity) approved by Legal and Revenue Ops and stored in the contract template repo.

A2: Security team provides canonical answers and evidence links for the top 40 questionnaire items; auto-fill script produces CSV/JSON exports compatible with vendor portals (SIG/Shared Assessments, OneTrust).
A3: Customer-facing evidence portal (read-only) with versioned SOC2 artifacts, a FAQ, and a dynamic checklist is accessible via a secure short-lived link; Security approves RBAC and audit logging.

A4: Integration runbook documenting how Sales can attach a pricing addendum and generate the evidence link during deal desk review; measured reduction in cycle time >=30% on sample deals within 30 days of rollout.
A5: Legal and Security sign-off approvals recorded in the ticket and linked PR(s) merged to templates repo.
A6: Telemetry: track events for "pricing_addendum_attached" and "evidence_portal_generated" with counts surfaced in Console's Deal Desk dashboard.
A7: No PII or secret keys exposed in the public evidence links; penetration test checklist item completed and passed.
A8: Rollout doc and Sales training slides published to Confluence/Drive.
A9: Backfill: mechanism to retroactively attach approved addendum to existing in-flight deals documented.
implementation_steps: Step 1: Workshop with Legal, Security, Revenue Ops, and Sales on 2026-03-12 to finalize pricing band definitions and required contract clauses.
Step 2: Security to produce canonical answers and evidence snippets for the top 40 questionnaire items by 2026-03-19.
Step 3: Engineering (Platform Integrations) to build an "Auto-Answer Export" that converts canonical answers into SIG format and OneTrust uploadable CSV. Deliver prototype by 2026-03-26.
Step 4: Template owner (Legal) drafts 3 pricing addenda and opens a GitHub PR; include version tags and change log. Target PR by 2026-03-22.

Step 5: Build a lightweight evidence portal (static site served from internal CDN) that exposes read-only links and a time-limited token generator for Sales. Security to review token gating and audit logs. Prototype by 2026-03-29.
Step 6: Revenue Ops updates Deal Desk process and builds a small web UI in Console for attaching addenda + generating evidence link; QA with Sales. Target integration 2026-04-05.
Step 7: Legal + Security reviews, integration tests, and pen-test checklist. Complete sign-offs by 2026-04-10.
Step 8: Publish rollout materials and run two Sales office hours for adoption. Go-live 2026-04-15.
Step 9: Post-launch: measure metrics for 30 days and iterate. Collect feedback via a short survey attached to generated evidence links.
Step 10: Plan to expand auto-answers beyond top 40 questions in Q3 based on adoption.
